title: Documented secret key value under a public or ordinary field label
summary: A synthetic Stripe sandbox secret-key-shaped value (sk_test_) sits under a field named publishable_key, under an ordinary field (name), under a deeply nested display label, beside a visibility:public field and under a NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment name. The value bytes are the same across the fixtures; only the label, nesting or carrier changes.
rationale: A label is the writer's claim about a value and may be wrong or misleading. A value whose own documented grammar names it a secret key stays a secret whatever the label says, and a recogniser that trusts the label would leave it exposed or report only part of it. The value class follows from the prefix the provider documents; the exact span is the value alone.

expectation.rationale: Flagged, with the span on the value only. The provider documents the prefix families and says secret keys are not safe to expose, so the value's class is a property of the value (the step a reviewer can repeat: prefix -> documented key type -> not safe to expose). No provider page states anything about field labels; that the label does not change the class is this inference, not a provider rule. The values are synthetic and non-issuable (see the fixture set notes); Stripe documents that sandbox keys start with sk_test_ for secret keys; no body length or alphabet claim is made here, and the values are never issued. Supabase secret-key positives are deliberately absent: provider-shaped sb_secret_ values are rejected by the host's push protection, so a Supabase secret positive needs a maintainer decision on how to carry one (see PR notes).

sources.supports: Key types table: a secret API key (sk_...) is 'Safe to expose: No' and has unrestricted permissions on all Stripe APIs; 'Only publishable keys are safe to expose outside your application's backend.'

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
